chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Nuh, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Qutaybah al-A'shi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It suffices for the believer as divine aid that he sees his enemy engaged in disobedience to God.
ai.seo_question: What is considered sufficient divine aid for a believer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), framing divine aid not merely as material victory but as the spiritual disarray of the adversary through their own sins. This reflects the Shia concept of *Nasr* (victory) where the enemy's deviation from divine law serves as a tangible sign of God's favor and protection over the faithful. It underscores that the believer's sufficiency lies in recognizing these subtle signs of divine support amidst worldly struggles.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-96 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Ayoob ibn Nooh, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Qutaybat al-A’eshi that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,
“It suffices for a believer to see God’s aid in the form of his enemies engaged in the Almighty God’s disobedience.”
